problem_text:
A maritime logistics company must devise a procurement and storage strategy for a critical fuel additive across a voyage schedule spanning 13 consecutive port calls.  
The initial stock of the additive in the ship’s storage tanks at the commencement of the voyage schedule is 46 kiloliters.  
At each port call \( t = 1, \dots, 13 \), the supplier permits the company to place a refueling request, the volume of which must be between 16 and 33 kiloliters.  
However, due to supply-chain delays, every requested shipment requires 4 days to be delivered and thus cannot be utilized to meet consumption or replenish tank levels until after that transit period.  
The anticipated consumption of the additive at each port call is specified as follows:  

* Port call 1: 53 kiloliters  
* Port call 2: 60 kiloliters  
* Port call 3: 34 kiloliters  
* Port call 4: 60 kiloliters  
* Port call 5: 11 kiloliters  
* Port call 6: 36 kiloliters  
* Port call 7: 37 kiloliters  
* Port call 8: 46 kiloliters  
* Port call 9: 53 kiloliters  
* Port call 10: 31 kiloliters  
* Port call 11: 55 kiloliters  
* Port call 12: 25 kiloliters  
* Port call 13: 18 kiloliters  

Consumption shortfalls are permissible, but any unmet demand is simply lost and will not be carried forward.  
Throughout the voyage schedule, additive volumes may be treated as continuous quantities, and the total quantity stored in the ship’s tanks at any moment must not surpass the tank capacity of 46 kiloliters.  
The total expenditure over the planning horizon comprises three elements: the procurement cost, amounting to 4 per kiloliter ordered; the storage cost, equaling 1 per kiloliter of additive kept in tanks from one port call to the next; and the penalty for shortfall, assessed at 8 per kiloliter of unmet consumption.  
The objective is to ascertain the optimal refueling volume for each port call and to monitor the ensuing tank levels and shortage quantities so as to minimize the total expenditure.
